instructions.task: Charity-donation chat: a persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate to Save the Children. Tag the final 'Persuader message to tag' with the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses.
notes: Earlier chat lines are context only and may be out of order.
Judge the tagged message's main function; if a greeting is attached to real content, tag the content.

criteria.greeting: Pure greeting with no other content: hello/hi, 'how are you', or the persuader's 'I'm good, how about you?' reply in the opening exchange.
criteria.charity_description: States facts about Save the Children itself: what it does, its programs, where it works, its mission, history or founder, or answers 'what do they do?'.
criteria.charity_trust: Introduces or names the charity, vouches for it, or praises it: reputation, ratings, trustworthiness, share of money going to programs, celebrities, its website or a URL.
criteria.suffering_facts: Describes children's suffering: death, hunger, war or abuse statistics, children being killed or starving, or a story about a particular child or family in need, even when framed as what a donation can help.
criteria.evoke_feelings: Tries to make the persuadee feel sympathy, sadness, guilt or warmth: 'the children need you', 'imagine...', 'you will feel great helping', the persuader voicing sadness about the children.
criteria.impact_reasoning: Reasons or argues that donating makes sense or has impact: 'your donation will make a big difference', 'they can only help when people donate', 'if everyone gave a nickel...', moral arguments such as 'children are our future' or 'everyone deserves a chance', and conceding an objection to argue back ('I know it is hard to trust people, but think of it this way', 'we all have struggles, but theirs are on another level').
criteria.small_amount_helps: Stresses that even a small amount is enough or helps, using words like 'even', 'as little as', 'just', 'won't miss', 'doesn't take much': 'every little bit helps', 'as little as $1 can feed a child', 'you can do as little as 5 cents', '$2 you won't miss', 'it doesn't have to be a full donation', 'we can all donate a little bit'. A plain statement of what an amount achieves, without stressing its smallness, is impact_reasoning.
criteria.persuader_donates: The persuader says they themselves donate, will donate, or will match the persuadee's donation.
criteria.persuader_story: The persuader narrates a past experience of their own or of someone they know (travels, work, a friend's loss) as a story of events. Mentioning what they are doing now or today is filler_or_admin.
criteria.donation_procedure: Explains how donating works: amount deducted from task payment, any amount from $0 to the full payment, the research team collects and sends it, payment methods, 'any amount is acceptable', 'you can judge it yourself', or the persuader plainly proposing a figure ('I was thinking a dollar to start with', 'may I suggest $.50 or $1').
criteria.asks_know_charity: Asks whether the persuadee has heard of or knows Save the Children or what they know about it.
criteria.asks_task_views: Asks the persuadee's opinions or experiences about donating, charities, children's causes or the issues ('do you donate to charities?', 'what do you think?', 'did you know 5 million children die...?').
criteria.asks_personal: Asks about the persuadee's personal life rather than about donating: do you have children, how is your life, your job, family, hobbies, whether they volunteer.
criteria.proposes_donation: Asks or urges the persuadee to donate at all: 'would you donate some of your payment?', 'would you consider donating?', 'we should donate to them!', 'agree to contribute what you make from this task', 'we're asking people to give a small part of their payment'.
criteria.asks_amount: Asks how much the persuadee will donate, or directly asks whether they could give a specific amount ('could you afford fifteen cents?'). Asking them to give more than they already offered is filler_or_admin.
criteria.thanks: Thanks the persuadee (for time, for donating, for chatting).
criteria.praises_user: Compliments the persuadee or their generosity ('that's awesome and generous', 'people like you make the world better', 'I feel so good working with you'), or a bare 'Great!'/'Awesome!' reacting to the persuadee agreeing or offering to donate.
criteria.acknowledges: Purely a reaction to or agreement with what the persuadee just said, with nothing further: 'I agree 100%', 'that's great to hear', 'I understand', 'that horrifies me'. Not when it concedes a point and then argues ('I know..., but think of it this way'); that is impact_reasoning.
criteria.filler_or_admin: Filler or housekeeping with no persuasive strategy: 'ok', 'yes', 'fine', closings like 'have a great day', remarks about the HIT/chat itself, confirming the amount, asking them to give a little more, small talk, the persuader mentioning what they are doing today, or the persuader's passing remarks about their own knowledge or feelings that make no appeal ('I'm learning about this myself', 'it seems vaguely familiar', 'I would feel bad not telling you about the organization').
criteria.unrelated: Completely unrelated to the conversation, nonsense, or not in English.
